boards.title: Your First Weekend at Slippery Rock University of Pennsylvania, Shared as Cards
boards.description: A low-pressure, under-21-safe sequence of campus landmarks, recreation, arts, and student-life stops for getting oriented at SRU.

cards.title: Start at Old Main
cards.subtitle: Friday afternoon · campus orientation stop
cards.notes: Begin with the clock-tower landmark at 104 Maltby Avenue, then use the surrounding paths to orient yourself before choosing the rest of your route.
cards.short_summary: A clear visual starting point for a first campus walk.
cards.evidence_claim: SRU’s accessible campus map identifies Old Main as the University’s oldest structure, constructed in 1893, at 104 Maltby Avenue.
cards.access_notes: Administrative and student-services building; check posted building access before entering.

cards.title: Find the Campus Success Center
cards.subtitle: Friday afternoon · student-life base camp
cards.notes: Locate the Campus Success Center early so you know where to return for lounges, student organizations, campus dining, and the building’s theater.
cards.short_summary: A practical stop for locating several student-facing services.
cards.evidence_claim: SRU’s accessible campus map describes the Campus Success Center as a gathering place and lists a ballroom, theater, student-organization offices, lounges, bookstore, coffee shop, and campus dining.
cards.access_notes: Public-facing building functions vary; use the campus map and posted information for current access.

cards.title: Pause in Smith Student Center
cards.subtitle: Friday afternoon · make a plan
cards.notes: Use the third floor near the Ballroom entrance as a calm planning pause: save campus contacts, compare weekend listings, and decide which nearby stop comes next.
cards.short_summary: A documented indoor study spot inside the student center.
cards.evidence_claim: SRU’s study-spaces article identifies the third floor of Smith Student Center near the Ballroom entrance as a quiet, comfortable space with a campus view.
cards.source_title: Ten best places to study on SRU’s campus
cards.access_notes: Study-space availability depends on building access and scheduled events.

cards.title: Settle into Bailey Library
cards.subtitle: Friday afternoon · study and reset
cards.notes: Take a short reset in the library, then identify a useful service desk or study area for the week ahead instead of trying to memorize every campus resource.
cards.short_summary: A reliable academic stop to add to an orientation walk.
cards.evidence_claim: SRU’s campus study-spaces article includes the library among its recommended campus study locations.
cards.source_title: Ten best places to study on SRU’s campus
cards.access_notes: Check current library access and service hours before visiting.

cards.title: Look for a Miller Theater performance
cards.subtitle: Friday evening · arts option
cards.notes: Check the current performance calendar, then make note of Miller Theater for a future concert, dance event, or theatrical performance that fits your schedule.
cards.short_summary: SRU’s main performing-arts venue is an easy cultural reference point.
cards.evidence_claim: SRU’s accessible campus map states that the Performing Arts Center includes Miller Theater, a 753-seat performance space with an orchestra pit.
cards.access_notes: Performance admission and venue access depend on the individual event; consult the event listing.

cards.title: Try the ARC
cards.subtitle: Friday evening · active indoor stop
cards.notes: Bring student identification and choose one easy activity, such as walking the indoor track or checking out the climbing wall, courts, or pool area.
cards.short_summary: A campus recreation stop with several indoor activity options.
cards.evidence_claim: SRU’s 2026–27 catalog says the ARC has a fitness center, five gymnasiums, indoor track, climbing wall, swimming pool, and group-fitness studios.
cards.access_notes: Traditional-program students receive access through the recreation-center fee; other visitors may need membership or a pass.

cards.title: Walk by the MAC fields
cards.subtitle: Saturday morning · outdoor orientation
cards.notes: Make the McFarland Outdoor Recreation Complex part of a daylight walk, and use its fields as a reference point while learning the campus’s recreation side.
cards.short_summary: An outdoor recreation complex with multipurpose and softball fields.
cards.evidence_claim: SRU’s 2026–27 catalog states that the McFarland Outdoor Recreation Complex has four multipurpose fields and two softball fields.
cards.access_notes: Use outdoor areas only as permitted; organized recreation and events may reserve fields.

cards.title: See Hickory Corner Schoolhouse
cards.subtitle: Saturday afternoon · historic campus detail
cards.notes: Add this furnished one-room schoolhouse to a daylight campus walk and read its marker or map description as a compact introduction to SRU’s education history.
cards.short_summary: A preserved, map-listed historic schoolhouse on campus.
cards.evidence_claim: SRU’s accessible campus map says the University acquired Hickory Corner Schoolhouse in 1988 and dedicated the furnished building in 1989; it served Franklin Township from 1881 to 1963.
cards.access_notes: View from public campus paths; interior access may be limited to academic use.

cards.entity_name: Drs. Paul and Carolyn Carruth Rizza Hall
cards.title: Take the Carruth Rizza stairwell pause
cards.subtitle: Saturday afternoon · quiet campus view
cards.notes: If the building is open, use the seating areas at the stairwell tops for a short reset, then head back out with a clearer sense of the Main Street side of campus.
cards.short_summary: An indoor pause point with documented seating and a Main Street view.
cards.evidence_claim: SRU’s study-spaces article identifies cozy seating areas at the top of both Carruth Rizza Hall stairwells, including a west-side view overlooking Main Street.
cards.source_title: Ten best places to study on SRU’s campus
cards.access_notes: Interior access is subject to building hours and University operations.

cards.title: End by checking student activities
cards.subtitle: Sunday · choose a next step
cards.notes: Before the weekend ends, review current campus activities and select one under-21-safe event, arts program, intramural option, or organization to try during the term.
cards.short_summary: A practical bridge from a first weekend to ongoing campus involvement.
cards.evidence_claim: SRU’s Student Activities page describes arts events, intramural sports, campus recreation, outdoor adventure programs, and student organizations as campus-life options.
cards.access_notes: Programs and event schedules change; use SRU’s current listings before attending.
